title: Rav Huna bar Manoach
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rava’s student and afterward came before Rav Papa, as in [Taanit 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.9a.14): Rav Huna bar Manoach, Rav Shmuel bar Idi and Rav Chiyya of Vastanya used to be before Rava. When Rava died, they came before Rav Papa. Whenever he told them a teaching that did not seem reasonable to them, they would signal to one another. Rav Papa was distressed, and in his dream he was made to read: “And I cut off the three shepherds.” The next day, when they took leave of him, he said to them: “Let the Rabbis go in peace” (so it is in Ein Yaakov).

Likewise he spoke in the name of Rav Acha son of Rav Ika, as in [Megillah 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.25b.18), [Gittin 24a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.24a.6) and [Gittin 64b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.64b.8), Bava Kamma 58a (compare [Bava Kamma 58b:13-14](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.58b.13-14)), [Bava Metzia 71b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.71b.7), [Sanhedrin 42a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.42a.15) and [Bekhorot 28b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.28b.7) and 45b. In [Yevamot 43a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.43a.5) he spoke in the name of Rav Idi son of Rav Ika, and Hyman proposes Rav Acha; and in [Bava Kamma 22a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.22a.12) he spoke in Rav Ika’s name — Hyman proposes reading in the name of Rav Acha son of Rav Ika, as in Dikdukei Soferim’s reading.

Hyman cites Nazir 51a (compare [Nazir 51b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.51b.2)): “Rav Huna bar Manoach asked”; in [Gittin 51a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.51a.6) and [Menachot 101a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.101a.5) he raises objections; and in [Bava Kamma 19b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.19b.11) they said, “If he tied it — on what account is he liable? Rav Huna bar Manoach said: on account of his pit that rolls.”[^3][^4]

notes.text: Rava is the deceased first teacher and Papa is the later teacher distressed by the pupils’ gestures. Hyman’s Ein Yaakov ending does not itself assert that the three died. Acha/Idi/Ika transmission corrections remain his proposals.

The inspected story runs from Taanit 9a into 9b: Rava dies, the three pupils come before Papa, Papa is distressed, and the dream and farewell follow. The consulted text has בשלמא, whereas Hyman explicitly reports Ein Yaakov לשלמא; that exact Ein Yaakov edition was not inspected. The narrative does not state that the three died. Acha/Idi/Ika chain corrections remain Hyman’s proposals.

The Taanit narrative continues at 9b with the dream and farewell. The report stops at the farewell; Heilprin’s retelling adds that the dream came to pass. The inspected transmission passages give Acha, Idi and Ika at the respective places, beside Hyman’s proposed uniform reading. See also [Taanit 9b continuation](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.9b.1). See [Heilprin’s corresponding entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=989&lang=en).

In the linked Bava Kamma passage, Huna bar Manoach first objects and then transmits a rule for valuing damage in Rav Acha son of Rav Ika’s name. In the linked Nazir passage, Rav Acha asks about skin; Huna bar Manoach asks about phlegm and spittle.
